A1.justification: Both complete 32-page PDFs describe MONET and contain corresponding main sections and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original MONET benchmark evaluations, knowledge-masking and toxicity experiments, ablations, and qualitative expert analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, expert-removal experiments, Appendix C ablations, and Appendix F multimodal examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same horizontal and vertical expert decompositions, routing procedures, auxiliary losses, and implementation algorithms. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including FineWeb-Edu, StarCoder, the language benchmarks, MULTIPL-E, RealToxicityPrompts, ToxiGen, and the CC3M vision-language examples in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains LLAMA, OLMoE, and Gemma 2 with and without Gemma Scope SAEs. Figure 3 and Tables 12–14 retain the same domain-masking comparators.

E3.justification: MONET's 100B-token pretraining budgets, model configurations, zero-shot and five-shot evaluations, masking criteria, and code/toxicity generation settings remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same auxiliary-loss and routing-group ablations. Domain/language masking, toxicity-threshold analyses, and qualitative case studies in Appendices D–F also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and generation-sampling descriptions. Neither adds training-seed variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports MONET-VD 1.4B averages of 0.478 for zero-shot and 0.510 for five-shot evaluation in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–31, the vertical-decomposition derivation, and Appendix A's complexity calculations are mathematically unchanged. The observed equation-spacing adjustments are typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable monosemantic experts, interpretability, and selective knowledge manipulation without degrading general performance.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and applicability claims are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning basic expert-selection criteria, qualitative-only automated interpretation, and knowledge manipulation restricted to unlearning.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3 and B retain the same JAX/Flax implementations, model configurations, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures. The documented code and checkpoint access information also remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to SAEs, conventional MoE architectures, and PEER are unchanged. Reference entries shift between pages but are not added or removed.

P1.justification: The header changes from 'Under review' to 'Published', and the arXiv version/date updates. Page 11 expands funding acknowledgements and revises grant identifiers; the research prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded acknowledgements reflow references across pages 11–15. Figure 2 and some equations receive small spacing adjustments, while all figures, tables, captions, and substantive visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication status, expands funding attribution, and makes minor typesetting adjustments. Methods, empirical evidence, mathematical reasoning, limitations, and reproducibility information remain intact, so these edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
